extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, representatives, and EPO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Official EPO Guidelines giving instructions on the practice and procedure to be followed in examination of European patent applications and patents under the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations. The Guidelines are organised in Parts A–H covering formalities, search, substantive examination, opposition, procedural matters, application requirements, patentability and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination (Part A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Formalities Examination: outlines the procedures for formalities examination, mainly with regard to grant proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A sets out procedures to be followed in formalities examination during grant proceedings. It contains instructions on formal requirements and related procedural steps examiners and applicants must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search (Part B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Search: deals with search matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B provides guidance on conducting searches for prior art and preparing search reports in accordance with EPC practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural aspects of substantive examination (Part C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Procedural Aspects of Substantive Examination: relates to procedures to be followed in examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C explains procedural steps and practices during substantive examination of European patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and limitation/revocation procedures (Part D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Opposition and Limitation/Revocation Procedures: relates to procedures to be followed in opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part D contains procedural guidance for oppositions, limitation and revocation, including how these proceedings are conducted before the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: General procedural matters (Part E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on General Procedural Matters: summarizes procedural matters relevant to several or all stages in proceedings before the EPO and contains information applicable to Euro‑PCT applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part E covers cross-cutting procedural issues, matters relevant at multiple stages of EPO proceedings, and the procedure before the EPO as designated or elected Office for Euro‑PCT applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements other than patentability (Part F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part F defines requirements which the application must fulfil other than patentability, in particular unity of invention (Article 82), sufficiency of disclosure (Article 83), clarity (Article 84) and the right to priority (Article 87 to Article 89).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F details non-patentability requirements that applications must meet; examiners assess these requirements under the cited EPC articles when examining applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Article 82)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention: a requirement the application must fulfil (Article 82).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered in Part F as a formal/substantive requirement; guidance relates to how to assess whether an application relates to one invention or a group of inventions linked so as to form a single general inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Article 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiency of disclosure: the application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art (Article 83).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F gives instructions to examiners on assessing whether the disclosure is enabling across the claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (Article 84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity: claims must be clear and concise and supported by the description (Article 84).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in Part F describes how to evaluate claim wording, clarity issues and support by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority (Articles 87–89)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to priority: rules governing claiming priority from earlier applications (Articles 87 to 89).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F explains requirements and formalities for claiming priority and how priority affects novelty and entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Part G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part G deals with the requirements of patentability provided for in Article 52 to Article 57, in particular exclusions from patentability (Article 52(2) and Article 53), novelty (Article 54), inventive step (Article 56) and industrial application (Article 57).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G provides substantive guidance to examiners on applying EPC patentability criteria when assessing whether claims meet the statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from patentability (Article 52(2) and Article 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions from patentability as set out in the EPC (e.g., Article 52(2) and Article 53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G explains which subject-matter is excluded from patentability and how to apply exclusion provisions, including principles for computer-implemented inventions and other excluded categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Article 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty: assessment of whether claimed subject-matter is new (Article 54).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G gives instructions on evaluating prior art, state of the art, public availability and how novelty is determined for claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Article 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step: assessment of whether claimed subject-matter involves an inventive step (Article 56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G includes methods and case law-based guidance for assessing inventive step (non-obviousness), including problem-solution approach and relevant comparisons with prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Article 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial application: requirement that the invention be capable of industrial application (Article 57).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G explains how to determine whether an invention can be made or used in any kind of industry and how this affects patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and corrections — admissibility (Part H; Rule 80 and Rule 137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part H deals with requirements relating to amendments and corrections, in particular questions of admissibility (Rule 80 and Rule 137).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance describes when amendments/corrections are admissible during different stages (e.g., during proceedings before the Examining Division or Opposition Division) and the application of Rules 80 and 137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and corrections — compliance with Article 123(2) & (3), Rule 139 and Rule 140 (Part H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part H addresses compliance with Article 123(2) and (3) EPC, Rule 139 and Rule 140 concerning added subject‑matter, extension of protection, and correction of errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H provides criteria for assessing whether amendments add subject-matter, extend protection, or correct errors, and explains procedural steps for implementing corrections and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the EPC and Implementing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines give instructions on practice and procedure to be followed in the various aspects of the examination of European applications and patents in accordance with the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall requirement: examination and procedural practice must conform with the EPC and Implementing Regulations; the Guidelines interpret and operationalise those legal provisions for examiners and users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer‑implemented inventions (CII) index and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The HTML and PDF versions contain an index dedicated to computer‑implemented inventions (CII), with a collection of direct hyperlinks to the relevant chapters in the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated CII index points to specific chapters and guidance on how to assess computer‑implemented inventions under EPC patentability and exclusion criteria (see Part G and related sections).
